meal.title: Detect a Tie in Rock‑Paper‑Scissors
meal.objective: You can recognise when both players chose the same move and print a tie message

voice.script: What happens when both players pick the same move? How do we detect a tie in rock‑paper‑scissors? You need to recognise a tie condition. In Python the equality operator checks whether two values match. If they match, we use print displays a message on the screen. So we write: if user_choice is equal to computer_choice: print('It’s a tie!') That line prints the tie message. Now the program will tell the player when the round ends in a tie. A tie is detected by comparing the two choices and printing a message. Modify the program to also announce a win for the player.

visual.code:
import random
moves = ['rock', 'paper', 'scissors']
user_choice = input('Your move: ')
computer_choice = random.choice(moves)
if user_choice == computer_choice:
    print('It’s a tie!')
else:
    print('Not a tie')
